rows.stem: If for any event E, \(P(E) + P(\overline{E}) = q\), then the value of \(q^2 - 3\) is :
rows.solution:
For any event E, \(P(E) + P(\overline{E}) = 1\), so \(q = 1\).

Then \(q^2 - 3 = 1 - 3 = -2\), which is option (B) \(-2\).

rows.stem: If \(\sin\theta = \cos\theta\ (0^\circ < \theta < 90^\circ)\), then the value of \(\sec\theta \cdot \sin\theta\) is :
rows.solution:
\(\sin\theta = \cos\theta\) with \(0^\circ < \theta < 90^\circ\) gives \(\tan\theta = 1\), so \(\theta = 45^\circ\).

\(\sec\theta \cdot \sin\theta = \dfrac{\sin\theta}{\cos\theta} = \tan\theta = 1\), which is option (D) 1.

rows.stem: If an arc of a circle of diameter 10 cm subtends an angle of \(144^\circ\) at the centre of the circle, then the length of the arc is :
rows.solution:
The radius is \(\dfrac{10}{2} = 5\) cm.

Arc length \(= \dfrac{144}{360} \times 2\pi \times 5 = \dfrac{2}{5} \times 10\pi = 4\pi\) cm, which is option (B) \(4\pi\) cm.

rows.stem: If \(a^b = 32\), where ‘a’ and ‘b’ are positive integers, then the value of \(b^{ab}\) is :
rows.solution:
\(32 = 2^5\), so take \(a = 2\) and \(b = 5\). Then \(ab = 10\) and \(b^{ab} = 5^{10}\).

(The only other way to write 32 as a positive-integer power is \(32^1\), which gives \(b^{ab} = 1^{32} = 1\); that value is not among the choices, so the question intends \(a = 2\), \(b = 5\).) This is option (B) \(5^{10}\).

rows.subtopic: Zeroes and Coefficients of a Quadratic Polynomial
rows.stem: If one zero of the polynomial \(q(x) = (p^2 + 4)x^2 + 65x + 4p\) is reciprocal of the other, then the value of ‘p’ is :
rows.solution:
If one zero is the reciprocal of the other, their product is 1.

Product of zeroes \(= \dfrac{4p}{p^2 + 4} = 1\), so \(p^2 - 4p + 4 = 0\), that is \((p - 2)^2 = 0\) and \(p = 2\). This is option (D) 2.

rows.chapter: Pair of Linear Equations in Two Variables
rows.subtopic: Graphical Method and Nature of Solutions
rows.stem: The equation of a line parallel to y-axis and at a distance of 5 units to the right of y-axis is :
rows.solution: A line parallel to the y-axis has the form \(x = c\). Five units to the right of the y-axis means \(c = 5\), so the line is \(x = 5\). This is option (A) \(x = 5\).

rows.stem: In the given figure, \(\dfrac{PS}{SQ} = \dfrac{PT}{TR}\) and \(\angle PST = \angle PRQ\). Prove that \(\Delta PQR\) is an isosceles triangle.
rows.figureNote: REQUIRED - triangle PQR with S on PQ and T on PR, segment ST drawn and the angles PST and PRQ marked; that S and T lie on PQ and PR is shown only in the drawing. Page idx 14.
rows.solution:
In triangle PQR, S lies on PQ and T on PR, and \(\dfrac{PS}{SQ} = \dfrac{PT}{TR}\). By the converse of the Basic Proportionality Theorem, \(ST \parallel QR\).

So \(\angle PST = \angle PQR\) (corresponding angles).

It is given that \(\angle PST = \angle PRQ\), so \(\angle PQR = \angle PRQ\).

Sides opposite equal angles are equal, so \(PR = PQ\), and triangle PQR is isosceles.

rows.stem: In the given figure, \(\Delta ABE \cong \Delta ACD\). Prove that \(\Delta ADE \sim \Delta ABC\).
rows.figureNote: REQUIRED - triangle ABC with D on AB and E on AC, DE, BE and CD drawn; that D lies on AB and E on AC (so the angle at A is shared) is shown only in the drawing. Page idx 16.
rows.solution:
Since \(\Delta ABE \cong \Delta ACD\), the corresponding parts are equal: \(AE = AD\) ... (1) and \(AB = AC\) ... (2).

Dividing (1) by (2): \(\dfrac{AD}{AB} = \dfrac{AE}{AC}\).

In triangles ADE and ABC, the angle at A is common: \(\angle DAE = \angle BAC\).

The two sides including the common angle are proportional, so by the SAS similarity criterion \(\Delta ADE \sim \Delta ABC\).

\(\cot^2\theta = \operatorname{cosec}^2\theta - 1 = \left(x + \dfrac{1}{4x}\right)^2 - 1 = x^2 + \dfrac{1}{2} + \dfrac{1}{16x^2} - 1 = x^2 - \dfrac{1}{2} + \dfrac{1}{16x^2} = \left(x - \dfrac{1}{4x}\right)^2\).

So \(\cot\theta = x - \dfrac{1}{4x}\) or \(\cot\theta = \dfrac{1}{4x} - x\).

In the first case, \(\operatorname{cosec}\theta + \cot\theta = \left(x + \dfrac{1}{4x}\right) + \left(x - \dfrac{1}{4x}\right) = 2x\).

In the second case, \(\operatorname{cosec}\theta + \cot\theta = \left(x + \dfrac{1}{4x}\right) + \left(\dfrac{1}{4x} - x\right) = \dfrac{1}{2x}\).

So \(\operatorname{cosec}\theta + \cot\theta = 2x\) or \(\dfrac{1}{2x}\).

rows.subtopic: Sum of First n Terms of an AP
rows.stem: Find the sum of all 3-digit natural numbers which are divisible by 11.
rows.solution:
The 3-digit multiples of 11 are \(110, 121, 132, \ldots, 990\), an AP with first term \(a = 110\) and common difference \(d = 11\).

\(a_n = 990\): \(110 + (n - 1) \times 11 = 990\), so \(n - 1 = 80\) and \(n = 81\).

\(S_{81} = \dfrac{81}{2}(110 + 990) = \dfrac{81}{2} \times 1100 = 44550\).

The sum of all 3-digit natural numbers divisible by 11 is 44550.

rows.subtopic: Solving a Quadratic Equation by Factorisation
rows.stem: The numerator of a fraction is 3 less than its denominator. If 2 is added to both numerator and denominator, then the sum of the new fraction and the original fraction is \(1\dfrac{9}{20}\). Find the original fraction.
rows.solution:
Let the denominator be x, so the numerator is \(x - 3\) and the fraction is \(\dfrac{x - 3}{x}\). Adding 2 to both gives \(\dfrac{x - 1}{x + 2}\).

Since \(1\dfrac{9}{20} = \dfrac{29}{20}\): \(\dfrac{x - 3}{x} + \dfrac{x - 1}{x + 2} = \dfrac{29}{20}\).

\(20\big[(x - 3)(x + 2) + x(x - 1)\big] = 29x(x + 2)\), so \(20(2x^2 - 2x - 6) = 29x^2 + 58x\), that is \(11x^2 - 98x - 120 = 0\).

\((x - 10)(11x + 12) = 0\), so \(x = 10\) (the denominator here is a positive whole number, so \(x = -\dfrac{12}{11}\) is rejected).

The original fraction is \(\dfrac{7}{10}\). (Check: \(\dfrac{7}{10} + \dfrac{9}{12} = 0{\cdot}7 + 0{\cdot}75 = 1{\cdot}45 = 1\dfrac{9}{20}\).)

rows.subtopic: Solving a Quadratic Equation by Factorisation
rows.stem: A train travelling at a uniform speed for 360 km would have taken 48 minutes less to travel the same distance if its speed were 5 km/h more. Find the original speed of the train.
rows.solution:
Let the original speed be x km/h. The time saved at \((x + 5)\) km/h is 48 minutes, that is \(\dfrac{48}{60} = \dfrac{4}{5}\) hour:

\(\dfrac{360}{x} - \dfrac{360}{x + 5} = \dfrac{4}{5}\).

\(\dfrac{360 \times 5}{x(x + 5)} = \dfrac{4}{5}\), so \(x(x + 5) = 2250\), that is \(x^2 + 5x - 2250 = 0\).

\((x + 50)(x - 45) = 0\), so \(x = 45\) (a speed cannot be negative).

The original speed of the train is 45 km/h. (Check: 360 km takes 8 hours at 45 km/h and 7.2 hours at 50 km/h, a difference of 0.8 hour, which is 48 minutes.)
